# SURAKSHA Disaster Intelligence Platform # Technical Specification: Flood Model Subsystem (Module 01) **Document Version**: 1.0.0 **Status**: APPROVED BASELINE SPECIFICATION **Module Identifier**: `SURAKSHA-MOD-01-FLOOD` **Target Delivery**: SURAKSHA Alpha / Phase 1 --- ## Executive Definition > **The SURAKSHA Flood Model is a LangGraph-orchestrated, multi-agent flood-intelligence pipeline that combines continuous hydrological forecasting, satellite/geospatial analysis, vulnerability modelling, and impact assessment to produce a standardized `FloodState` for the central SURAKSHA backend.** The **Flood Model is not a single machine learning model**. It is a complete disaster-specific intelligence pipeline. As the first specialized hazard module built for SURAKSHA, it establishes the architectural contract, multi-agent pattern, and state schema that will subsequently be replicated for Earthquakes, Landslides, Cyclones, Wildfires, and Tsunamis. ``` SURAKSHA Multi-Hazard Architecture │ ├── Flood Model [MODULE 01 — ACTIVE SPECIFICATION] ├── Earthquake Model [MODULE 02 — PLANNED] ├── Landslide Model [MODULE 03 — PLANNED] ├── Cyclone Model [MODULE 04 — PLANNED] ├── Wildfire Model [MODULE 05 — PLANNED] └── Tsunami Model [MODULE 06 — PLANNED] ``` --- ## 1. Core Objectives & Intelligence Chain The Flood Model systematically answers four foundational operational questions in strict chronological order: ``` ┌─────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ A. What is happening? │ ───> │ B. What may happen next?│ │ Detection & Condition │ │ Forecasting │ └─────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌─────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ C. How risky is it? │ ───> │ D. What is affected? │ │ Risk Assessment │ │ Impact Assessment │ └─────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ ``` 1. **Detection / Current Condition**: What are the current river gauge stages, rainfall accumulation rates, soil moisture levels, and surface water extents? 2. **Forecasting**: How will runoff, discharge rates, and inundation depths propagate over the next 6, 12, 24, and 72 hours? 3. **Risk Assessment**: Given the forecast, local terrain, and historical district vulnerabilities, what is the probability and severity of critical threshold breaches? 4. **Impact Assessment**: What critical infrastructure (roads, bridges, schools, hospitals), population clusters, agricultural zones, and shelters fall within the flood polygon? --- ## 2. End-to-End Pipeline Architecture The Flood Model executes as an explicit, deterministic directed acyclic graph (DAG) managed via **LangGraph**. The workflow enforces parallel sensory ingest followed by sequential analytical aggregation: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph SENSORY_TIER ["1. SENSORY & INGESTION TIER (Parallel Execution)"] direction LR RawIn["Raw Ingestion Feeds
(Sensors / APIs / Streams)"] --> DataAgent["Data Agent
• Schema Validation
• Cleaning & Normalization
• Health & Quality Checks"] WeatherFeed["Weather APIs / Radar
(IMD / GFS / ECMWF)"] --> WeatherAgent["Weather Agent
• Precipitation Aggregation
• Storm Hyetographs
• Forecast Met-Features"] EarthObs["Google Earth Engine / SAR
(Sentinel-1 / Sentinel-2)"] --> SatAgent["Satellite Agent
• Cloud Masking & Calib
• SAR Backscatter Otsu
• Surface Water Change"] end subgraph PREDICTION_TIER ["2. PREDICTION & ANALYTICS TIER (Sequential Processing)"] direction TB DataAgent & WeatherAgent --> ForecastAgent["Forecast Agent
• Baseline: Persistence & ARIMA
• Causal Recurrent: GRU / LSTM
• Exogenous Rain Encoder: BiLSTM
• Multi-step Stage Forecast"] ForecastAgent & DataAgent --> RiskAgent["Risk Agent (XGBoost / LightGBM)
• Dynamic Forecast Features
• Static Priors (DFSI / Area / Impact)
• Computes: Risk Score (0-1) & Severity"] RiskAgent & SatAgent --> ImpactAgent["Impact Agent (PostGIS + GEE)
• Flood Polygon Overlays
• Infrastructure Exposure Analysis
• Population & Shelter Proximity"] end subgraph STATE_TIER ["3. STANDARDIZED STATE CONTRACT"] ImpactAgent --> FloodState["Standardized FloodState
(Pydantic V2 / JSON Contract)"] end SENSORY_TIER --> PREDICTION_TIER PREDICTION_TIER --> STATE_TIER ``` --- ## 3. Data Tiering & Taxonomy Data inputs are segregated into four distinct categories to avoid conflating static vulnerability priors with dynamic continuous time series: ``` FLOOD DATA TAXONOMY │ ┌──────────────────┬───────────────┴───────────────┬──────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Category A: Category B: Category C: Category D: Hydrological Series Historical Prior Catalog Geospatial / EO External Weather (Dynamic 1D/2D) (Regional Tables) (Earth Engine) (Meteo Feeds) - Stage Heights - DFSI.csv (744 districts) - Sentinel-1 SAR - Radar hyetographs - Discharge rates - FloodedArea.csv (732 dist) - Sentinel-2 Opt - Precipitation rate - 5-min urban mesh - FloodImpact.csv (732 dist) - NASADEM / SRTM - IMD/ECMWF forecasts - Stream gauge feeds - India_Flood_Inventory_v3.csv - Dynamic World - Soil saturation index ``` ### Category A: Hydrological Time Series (Dynamic) * **Purpose**: Direct sequential input for the `ForecastAgent`. * **Variables**: Continuous timestamp, river water level ($m$), volumetric discharge ($m^3/s$), precipitation intensity ($mm/h$), culvert/pipe flow ($m^3/s$). * **Primary Sources**: * `data/urban_flood/`: High-resolution 1D/2D urban benchmark (3,716 surface mesh cells + 17 subsurface drainage nodes at 5-minute sampling intervals). * Central Water Commission (CWC) telemetry APIs and state hydrometric gauge networks. ### Category B: Historical Flood Data & Tabular Priors (Static / Cross-Sectional) * **Purpose**: District-level baseline exposure weighting and historical incident replay. **Not suitable for continuous LSTM training**. * **Primary Assets**: * `DFSI.csv` (744 districts): District Flood Susceptibility Index ranking regional baseline hazard. * `District_FloodedArea.csv` (732 districts): Historical percentage of district inundated vs. permanent water bodies. * `District_FloodImpact.csv` (732 districts): Historical human fatalities, casualties, affected population, and mean duration. * `India_Flood_Inventory_v3.csv` (6,876 verified events): Longitudinal disaster catalog for verification, model calibration, and retrospective scenario replay. ### Category C: Satellite & Earth Observation Data (Spatial) * **Purpose**: Inundation surface delineation, ground-truth water boundary mapping, and terrain constraint extraction. * **Sources**: Google Earth Engine (GEE), Copernicus Open Access Hub, Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (C-band SAR, cloud-penetrating), Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI, optical), Copernicus DEM / ALOS PALSAR / NASADEM (30m elevation). ### Category D: External Weather & Hydrometeorological Feeds * **Purpose**: Antecedent precipitation indexing and exogenous future rainfall profiles. * **Sources**: India Meteorological Department (IMD) gridded rainfall / radar hyetographs, ECMWF Integrated Forecasting System (IFS), NOAA Global Forecast System (GFS), Open-Meteo High-Resolution APIs. --- ## 4. Multi-Agent Specification & Responsibilities ``` AGENT BOUNDARIES │ ┌─────────────────────────┬─────────┴─────────┬─────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Data Agent Weather Agent Satellite Agent Forecast Agent Ingestion, cleaning, Rainfall metrics, GEE SAR backscatter, ARIMA/GRU/LSTM, schema validation. hyetographs. flood extent mask. future water level. [NO RISK PREDICTION] [WEATHER ONLY] [SPATIAL ONLY] [TIME-SERIES ONLY] │ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────┼───────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘ ▼ Risk Agent XGBoost on dynamic forecast + static tabular priors. Outputs calibrated risk score (0.00-1.00) & severity. │ ▼ Impact Agent PostGIS intersections: roads, schools, shelters, people. ``` ### 4.1 Data Agent * **Role**: Deterministic gatekeeper of raw sensory telemetry. * **Explicit Boundary**: **Does NOT predict risk, forecast stages, or classify alerts.** * **Core Tasks**: * Ingest incoming sensor messages (MQTT, Kafka, REST webhooks, CSV drops). * Enforce schema compliance via Pydantic models. * Detect and log missing readings, anomalous jumps (sensor spike filtering), and clock drifts. * Perform min-max / z-score normalization based on historical gauge statistics. * Wrap all accepted data points into immutable `Evidence` records with cryptographic hashes and provenance timestamps. ### 4.2 Weather Agent * **Role**: Meteorologic feature aggregator and storm hyetograph generator. * **Core Tasks**: * Harvest real-time and forecasted cumulative precipitation across target catchments. * Compute Antecedent Precipitation Indices ($API_{3d}$, $API_{7d}$) for soil moisture saturation estimates. * Construct future rainfall profiles $[r_{t+1}, r_{t+2}, \dots, r_{t+H}]$ across the forecast horizon $H$. ### 4.3 Satellite Agent * **Role**: Earth Observation feature extractor and surface water change detector. * **Core Tasks**: * Query Google Earth Engine REST API / Python SDK for Sentinel-1 GRD SAR scenes covering the region of interest. * Apply speckle filtering (Lee filter, $7 \times 7$ window) and Otsu automatic thresholding on VV/VH backscatter ($\sigma_0 \le -16 \text{ dB}$). * Compute Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) and Modified NDWI (MNDWI) on cloud-free Sentinel-2 acquisitions. * Generate spatial differential masks: $\Delta \text{Extent} = \text{Water}_{\text{current}} - \text{Water}_{\text{permanent\_baseline}}$. * Emit standardized GeoJSON polygons containing confidence scores and acquisition timestamps. ### 4.4 Forecast Agent * **Role**: Causal sequence modeling of downstream stage heights and flood depths. * **Causality Enforcement**: * **Unidirectional (Causal) LSTM / GRU**: Mandatory for target water level prediction ($y_{t+1}, \dots, y_{t+H}$). Under live operations, unmeasured future stages cannot be read in reverse; backward passes over the forecast target induce catastrophic lookahead leakage. * **Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM)**: Strictly approved as an **Exogenous Rainfall Profile Encoder**. Because forecast storm hyetographs are fully known across the horizon from meteorological radar, a BiLSTM reads the entire storm curve forward and backward to encode peak storm intensity and duration before feeding the causal water depth decoder. * **Experimental Benchmarking Hierarchy**: 1. *Baseline 0*: Persistence Model ($y_{t+h} = y_t$). 2. *Baseline 1*: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). 3. *Baseline 2*: Seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA) for tidal or monsoon cycles. 4. *Deep Learning Tier*: 2-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). 5. *Deep Learning Tier*: 2-layer Causal LSTM ($H=24$ to $435$ steps). 6. *Hybrid Encoder-Decoder*: BiLSTM Rain Profile Encoder $\rightarrow$ Causal LSTM Water Forecaster. ### 4.5 Risk Agent * **Role**: Multi-modal fusion of dynamic hydrological forecasts and static socioeconomic priors. * **Model Engine**: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (**XGBoost / LightGBM**). * **Feature Vector ($X_{\text{risk}}$)**: * Dynamic Forecast Features: Maximum predicted water depth ($\max \hat{y}_{t+h}$), rate of stage rise ($\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta t}$), predicted duration above warning level. * Meteorological Features: 24-hour cumulative rainfall, storm intensity percentile. * Static Regional Priors: District Flood Susceptibility Index (`DFSI`), historical flooded area ratio (`Flooded Area %`), permanent water body buffer (`Permanent Water %`), historical casualty index (`District_FloodImpact`). * Spatial Evidence: Satellite-observed inundation expansion rate ($\Delta \text{Extent}$). * **Outputs**: Calibrated continuous risk score $R \in [0.00, 1.00]$, categorical severity (`LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, `CRITICAL`), and model epistemic confidence $C \in [0.00, 1.00]$. ### 4.6 Impact Agent * **Role**: Geospatial asset exposure, critical infrastructure intersection, and vulnerability mapping. * **Tech Stack**: PostGIS spatial database + Google Earth Engine + Shapely / GeoPandas. * **Core Tasks**: * Intersect predicted/observed flood polygons with OpenStreetMap (OSM) and Census spatial layers. * Quantify inundated geographic area ($\text{km}^2$) and identify breached district administrative boundaries. * Enumerate threatened infrastructure: bridges, substations, schools, hospitals, drinking water stations. * Calculate nearest unaffected emergency shelters and compute routing accessibility corridors. --- ## 5. Formal Data Contracts & State Schemas ### 5.1 The `Evidence` Object Every incoming observation, whether from a river gauge, radar station, or satellite pass, is packaged into an immutable `Evidence` record: ```json { "evidence_id": "evi-flood-20260921-00892", "source_type": "sensor_gauge | weather_radar | satellite_sar | crowdsource", "source_id": "CWC-GAUGE-GANGES-PATNA-04", "timestamp": "2026-09-21T21:40:00Z", "ingest_timestamp": "2026-09-21T21:42:15Z", "location": { "latitude": 25.612, "longitude": 85.144, "district": "Patna", "state": "Bihar" }, "metrics": { "water_level_m": 48.92, "danger_level_m": 48.60, "warning_level_m": 47.60, "discharge_m3s": 34200.0, "rainfall_last_1h_mm": 14.2 }, "quality_flag": "VALIDATED", "hash_sha256": "8f4a12b...c72e" } ``` ### 5.2 The Standardized `FloodState` Contract The final artifact produced by the Flood Subsystem that is delivered to SURAKSHA Core: ```json { "$schema": "https://suraksha.gov.in/schemas/v1/flood_state.json", "hazard_type": "flood", "state_id": "flstate-20260921-patna-001", "timestamp": "2026-09-21T21:45:00Z", "status": "UNDER_REVIEW", "location": { "district": "Patna", "state": "Bihar", "center_lat": 25.612, "center_lon": 85.144, "bounding_box": [85.01, 25.50, 85.25, 25.70] }, "current_condition": { "observed_water_level_m": 48.92, "danger_level_threshold_m": 48.60, "status": "ABOVE_DANGER_LEVEL" }, "forecast": { "model_architecture": "Hybrid_BiLSTM_RainEncoder_Causal_LSTM_Dec", "horizon_hours": 24, "predictions": [ {"step_hour": 6, "water_level_m": 49.35, "upper_bound_95": 49.60, "lower_bound_95": 49.10}, {"step_hour": 12, "water_level_m": 49.82, "upper_bound_95": 50.15, "lower_bound_95": 49.49}, {"step_hour": 24, "water_level_m": 50.10, "upper_bound_95": 50.55, "lower_bound_95": 49.65} ] }, "risk_assessment": { "risk_score": 0.88, "severity": "CRITICAL", "confidence": 0.92, "primary_risk_drivers": [ "Water level exceeding historical danger mark by +0.32m", "Catchment rainfall forecast indicates severe incoming convective cell (+65mm/12h)", "High baseline regional vulnerability (DFSI: 19.30, 92nd percentile)" ] }, "impact_assessment": { "affected_area_km2": 42.6, "affected_districts": ["Patna", "Vaishali"], "exposed_population_estimate": 142000, "critical_infrastructure_exposed": { "schools": 14, "hospitals": 3, "primary_health_centers": 8, "inundated_road_segments_km": 28.4 }, "nearest_operational_shelters": [ {"shelter_id": "SHELTER-PAT-09", "capacity": 1200, "current_occupancy": 150, "distance_km": 3.2}, {"shelter_id": "SHELTER-PAT-12", "capacity": 2500, "current_occupancy": 0, "distance_km": 5.8} ] }, "degraded_paths": [], "evidence_references": [ "evi-flood-20260921-00892", "evi-sat-s1-20260921-gee-034", "evi-imd-patna-radar-120" ], "model_version": "suraksha-flood-v1.2.0" } ``` --- ## 6. SURAKSHA Core Integration & Incident Lifecycle The Flood Model does not dispatch emergency workers, send public cell broadcasts, or update user interfaces directly. It emits the standardized `FloodState` into the SURAKSHA Core message bus: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Ingestion : Sensor / Weather / Satellite Trigger Ingestion --> FloodModelPipeline : LangGraph Multi-Agent Run FloodModelPipeline --> FloodStateEmitted : Produces FloodState state SURAKSHA_CORE { FloodStateEmitted --> UNDER_REVIEW : Threshold Breach (Risk > 0.65) UNDER_REVIEW --> VERIFIED : Disaster Officer / NDMA Validation UNDER_REVIEW --> REJECTED : False Positive / Sensor Malfunction VERIFIED --> ALERTED : CAP Protocol Generation ALERTED --> RESPONSE_ACTIVE : Incident Commander Activates NDRF/SDRF RESPONSE_ACTIVE --> RESOLVED : Water Level Recedes Below Warning } ALERTED --> PublicApp : Push Notification / Cell Broadcast ALERTED --> AuthorityDashboard : Situation Report (SITREP) RESPONSE_ACTIVE --> FieldWorkerMobile : Evacuation & Shelter Assignments RESOLVED --> [*] ``` ### Boundary Matrix: Flood Model vs. SURAKSHA Core | Capability / Concern | Flood Model Subsystem | SURAKSHA Core Platform | | :--- | :---: | :---: | | **Hydrological Time-Series Ingestion & Normalization** | **YES** | NO | | **Stage & Depth Forecasting (LSTM / GRU / ARIMA)** | **YES** | NO | | **Satellite Water Surface Delineation (GEE / SAR)** | **YES** | NO | | **Risk Score & Severity Computation (XGBoost)** | **YES** | NO | | **Geospatial Infrastructure Overlay (PostGIS)** | **YES** | NO | | **User Authentication & RBAC (Auth0 / Supabase / Neon Auth)** | NO | **YES** | | **Incident Lifecycle Management (`UNDER_REVIEW` $\rightarrow$ `ACTIVE`)** | NO | **YES** | | **Public Multi-lingual Alert Dissemination (SMS / CAP / WhatsApp)** | NO | **YES** | | **Rescue Worker & Vehicle Fleet Dispatch Logistics** | NO | **YES** | | **Shelter Bed Allocation & Relief Supply Inventory** | NO | **YES** | | **Citizen SOS Intake & Mobile App GraphQL / REST APIs** | NO | **YES** | --- ## 7. Role of Large Language Models (LLM Governance) To maintain scientific integrity and prevent catastrophic hallucinations in high-stakes public safety decisions: > [!CAUTION] > **The Large Language Model is strictly prohibited from participating in the quantitative numerical prediction chain.** ``` ❌ INCORRECT (UNGOVERNED / DANGEROUS): Raw Telemetry ───> LLM Prompts ───> "I predict water level will reach 52m, risk is CRITICAL!" ✅ CORRECT (SURAKSHA GOVERNANCE PATTERN): Raw Telemetry ───> Specialist Models ───> Verified Numbers ───> LLM Agent ───> Natural Language (ARIMA/LSTM/XGB) (Risk: 0.88, Conf: 0.92) SITREP & Briefing ``` * **Prohibited LLM Actions**: * Calculating or altering `water_level`, `risk_score`, `severity`, `confidence`, or `affected_area_km2`. * Overriding machine learning model outputs based on conversational prompts. * **Permitted LLM Actions**: * **Automated Situation Reports (SITREPs)**: Translating complex multi-agent JSON state contracts into concise, actionable prose for district magistrates. * **Multilingual Translation**: Converting verified alert bulletins into 22 scheduled Indian languages. * **Public Safety Guidance Narration**: Summarizing nearest shelter corridors for citizen mobile interfaces. --- ## 8. Failure Handling & Graceful Degradation Protocols In mission-critical disaster management, system components will encounter outages (cloud connectivity loss, satellite orbital revisit delays, sensor telemetry dropouts). The Flood Model enforces explicit fallback degradation without hallucinating missing data: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph FAIL_SCENARIOS ["Failure & Fallback Matrix"] E1["Google Earth Engine API Timeout / Quota Exhausted"] --> F1["Append 'satellite' to degraded_paths
Fallback: Rely on Gauge Hydrometry + DEM Contours
Confidence Penalty: -0.15"] E2["LSTM Model Memory OOM / CUDA Failure"] --> F2["Append 'lstm_forecaster' to degraded_paths
Fallback: Instant Hot-Swap to GRU or Linear ARIMA
Mark Forecast Bounds as 'Degraded Bounds'"] E3["Weather Radar API Inaccessible"] --> F3["Append 'weather_feed' to degraded_paths
Fallback: Use Cached 6-hour Runoff Persistence
Issue Warning: Precipitation Antecedent Only"] E4["Single River Gauge Telemetry Offline"] --> F4["Append 'gauge_drop:ID' to degraded_paths
Fallback: Kriging Spatial Interpolation from Adjacent Gauges
Record Source Flag: INTERPOLATED"] end ``` Every response contains the array `degraded_paths: []`. If any upstream sensory or analytical module fails, the degradation is explicitly listed, the overall `confidence` metric is penalised mathematically, and SURAKSHA Core is notified that the assessment was generated under degraded operational mode. --- ## 9. Machine Learning Experimentation & Validation Framework Model research must be empirical, reproducible, and benchmarked against standard hydrological baselines. ``` EXPERIMENTATION LADDER │ Level 0: Baseline ───> Persistence ($y_{t+h} = y_t$) Level 1: Linear ───> ARIMA / SARIMA Level 2: Recurrent───> Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) Level 3: Deep LSTM───> 2-Layer Causal LSTM Level 4: Hybrid ───> BiLSTM Storm Encoder + Causal LSTM Decoder ``` ### 9.1 Quantitative Evaluation Metrics All time-series models must be benchmarked across the continuous urban hydrodynamic test sequence (`data/urban_flood/`, 445 time steps) using: 1. **Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)**: Penalizes major peak stage discrepancies: $$\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}$$ 2. **Mean Absolute Error (MAE)**: Measures average continuous deviation: $$\text{MAE} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N |y_i - \hat{y}_i|$$ 3. **Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE)**: The universal standard in hydrological engineering: $$\text{NSE} = 1 - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - \bar{y})^2}$$ * $\text{NSE} = 1.0$: Perfect simulation. * $\text{NSE} > 0.75$: Excellent hydrological fit. * $\text{NSE} < 0.00$: Model is worse than predicting the historical mean $\bar{y}$. 4. **Lead-Time Degradation Curve**: Measuring metric degradation as horizon increases from $t+1\text{h}$ to $t+6\text{h}$, $t+12\text{h}$, and $t+24\text{h}$. 5. **Inference Latency Budget**: Maximum permitted inference latency per agent step: $\le 1,200 \text{ ms}$. --- ## 10. Implementation Codebase Structure The Flood Subsystem is organized into modular packages under the `flood/` root directory: ```text flood/ │ ├── __init__.py ├── flood_model.py # Master LangGraph entrypoint & execution pipeline ├── contracts/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── evidence.py # Pydantic schema for validated sensory evidence │ └── flood_state.py # Pydantic schema for standardized FloodState contract │ ├── agents/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── data_agent.py # Ingestion, validation, missing-value imputation │ ├── weather_agent.py # Rainfall indexing, storm hyetograph preparation │ ├── satellite_agent.py # GEE connection, SAR backscatter, flood masking │ ├── forecast_agent.py # Sequence modeling orchestration (ARIMA/GRU/LSTM) │ ├── risk_agent.py # XGBoost inference on dynamic forecast + priors │ └── impact_agent.py # PostGIS infrastructure & population overlay │ ├── graph/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── flood_graph.py # LangGraph StateGraph definition, nodes & routing edges │ └── fallback_router.py # Dynamic rerouting logic for degraded paths │ ├── models/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── baseline/ │ │ ├── persistence.py # Persistence baseline model │ │ └── arima_model.py # Auto-ARIMA & SARIMA wrappers │ ├── recurrent/ │ │ ├── gru_forecaster.py # 2-layer causal GRU implementation │ │ ├── lstm_forecaster.py # 2-layer causal LSTM implementation │ │ └── hybrid_bilstm_lstm.py # BiLSTM rain encoder + causal LSTM decoder │ └── risk/ │ ├── xgboost_risk.py # XGBoost classifier / regressor for hazard scoring │ └── tabular_features.py # Feature engineering for DFSI/FloodedArea/Impact │ ├── data/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── loaders/ │ │ ├── urban_flood_loader.py # Loader for 1D/2D pipe/street mesh dataset │ │ ├── regional_priors.py # Loader & parser for DFSI/FloodedArea/Impact CSVs │ │ └── inventory_catalog.py # Loader for India_Flood_Inventory_v3.csv │ └── preprocessing/ │ ├── scalers.py # Min-Max & Standard scalers for sequence arrays │ └── spatial_aligner.py # Coordinate & CRS projection harmonizer (EPSG:4326) │ ├── geospatial/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── earth_engine/ │ │ ├── auth.py # GEE service account authentication │ │ └── s1_sar_processor.py # Sentinel-1 SAR speckle filter & Otsu thresholding │ └── postgis/ │ ├── spatial_queries.py # ST_Intersects, ST_DWithin for infrastructure exposure │ └── osm_connector.py # OpenStreetMap school/hospital/shelter parser │ └── evaluation/ ├── __init__.py ├── metrics.py # Implementation of RMSE, MAE, NSE, Peak Error ├── benchmark_runner.py # Automated comparison across all model architectures └── replay_harness.py # Historical event replay using India Flood Inventory ``` --- ## 11. Engineering Work Breakdown Structure (Team Task Division) To facilitate parallel sprint execution across engineering disciplines, work is partitioned into 5 independent tracks: ``` ENGINEERING TRACK BREAKDOWN │ ┌──────────────┬──────────────┬─────────┴────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ Track 1 Track 2 Track 3 Track 4 Track 5 Track 6 Data & Prior Sequence ML Geospatial & GEE Risk & ML LangGraph Contracts & Engineers Researchers Engineers Engineers Architects Verification ``` ### Track 1: Data Ingestion & Prior Engineering * **Assignee**: Data / Backend Engineers * **Deliverables**: 1. High-throughput loaders for `data/urban_flood/` (1D pipes, 2D mesh, 5-minute timesteps). 2. Ingestion pipeline for `DFSI.csv`, `District_FloodedArea.csv`, `District_FloodImpact.csv`. 3. Replay loader for `India_Flood_Inventory_v3.csv` to feed simulation scenarios. 4. Unit tests verifying NaN handling, normalization bounds, and schema integrity. ### Track 2: Hydrological Forecasting & Sequence Modeling * **Assignee**: AI/ML Deep Learning Researchers * **Deliverables**: 1. Train and evaluate Persistence and ARIMA/SARIMA baselines. 2. Implement PyTorch 2-layer Causal GRU and Causal LSTM. 3. Implement Hybrid Architecture: BiLSTM future rainfall encoder paired with Causal LSTM stage decoder. 4. Compute RMSE, MAE, and Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) across all forecast horizons ($t+6, t+12, t+24$). ### Track 3: Satellite Earth Observation & Geospatial Analytics * **Assignee**: Geospatial / Remote Sensing Engineers * **Deliverables**: 1. Google Earth Engine automated query client for Sentinel-1 C-band SAR scenes. 2. Automatic Otsu thresholding and speckle filtering for water extent segmentation. 3. PostGIS spatial database schema and geometric intersection scripts for school, hospital, and shelter exposure. ### Track 4: Vulnerability Modeling & Risk Scoring * **Assignee**: Applied ML Engineers * **Deliverables**: 1. Feature store merging dynamic water forecasts with regional tabular priors. 2. Train and tune XGBoost / LightGBM model to predict risk score ($0.00-1.00$) and severity classes. 3. Implement model explainability (TreeSHAP) to surface `primary_risk_drivers`. ### Track 5: Orchestration, State Machine & Failure Degeneracy * **Assignee**: Senior Systems / Platform Engineers * **Deliverables**: 1. LangGraph `StateGraph` linking all agents into a deterministic, fault-tolerant DAG. 2. Fallback router handling degraded paths (GEE failure, sensor telemetry dropouts, LSTM memory errors). 3. Integration tests verifying end-to-end execution from raw input to `FloodState`. ### Track 6: SURAKSHA Core Handoff & Governance * **Assignee**: Backend / Security Leads * **Deliverables**: 1. Pydantic V2 data contracts (`Evidence`, `FloodState`). 2. Message bus publisher transmitting validated states to SURAKSHA Core incident lifecycle. 3. LLM narrative generation wrapper strictly operating on output `FloodState` without altering numerical fields. --- ## 12. Verification & Acceptance Criteria A build of the Flood Model Subsystem is certified for integration into SURAKSHA Core when it meets the following criteria: | Metric / Check | Required Acceptance Standard | Verification Method | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Temporal Causality** | Zero target lookahead leakage across all forecast horizons | Unit test inspecting gradient backpropagation graph | | **Hydrological Accuracy** | Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency $\text{NSE} \ge 0.75$ on benchmark test set | Automated run via `evaluation/benchmark_runner.py` | | **Risk Calibration** | Area Under ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) $\ge 0.88$ on historical inventory replay | `evaluation/replay_harness.py` against 6,876 events | | **Fault Resilience** | 100% graceful completion under injected GEE or LSTM failures | Chaos integration test verifying `degraded_paths` logging | | **Inference Latency** | Full LangGraph execution pipeline $\le 3.5 \text{ seconds}$ | Benchmark latency profile under concurrent load | | **Contract Validity** | Zero schema validation errors against Pydantic `FloodState` | Strict runtime validation gate | --- **Approved By**: Lead AI/ML Systems Engineer & Technical Architect **Distribution**: SURAKSHA Engineering, ML Research, and Geospatial Data Teams

# Architecture Decision Record: ADR-001 Modular Monolith Architecture

## Metadata
- **Status**: `VERIFIED`
- **Deciders**: `SURAKSHA Core Architecture Team`
- **Date**: `2026-11-21`
- **Technical Context**: `Platform Core vs. Hazard Subsystems Topology`

---

## 1. Context & Problem Statement
SURAKSHA requires an architectural topology capable of coordinating complex, multi-agent scientific pipelines across real-time hydrological data ingestion, deep learning inference, geospatial raster processing, and civil defense alerting. The system must support high-speed execution under emergency conditions, allow offline-first air-gapped deployment, and enable clean modular addition of future disaster modules (e.g. cyclone, earthquake) without architectural fragmentation.

---

## 2. Alternatives Considered
1. **Distributed Microservices**:
   * *Description*: Deploying separate containerized services for telemetry ingestion, neural forecasting, satellite processing, Jev supervision, and alerting communicating via gRPC/HTTP.
   * *Drawbacks*: Severe operational overhead, network latency penalties across large in-memory tensors and GeoJSON geometries, network partition risks during disaster conditions, complex local testing.
2. **Loosely Coupled Scripts / Notebooks**:
   * *Description*: Standalone Python scripts executed by cron jobs.
   * *Drawbacks*: Lack of shared typed state contracts, zero supervisory verification, race conditions, brittle failure recovery.
3. **Modular Monolith (Chosen)**:
   * *Description*: A unified Python codebase strictly partitioned into two layers: `suraksha.core` (zero disaster logic, generic contracts, geospatial abstractions) and `suraksha.disasters.<hazard>` (independent hazard plugins registering via `HazardRegistry`).

---

## 3. Decision & Justification
We adopted the **Modular Monolith** architecture:
* **Zero Inter-Process Latency**: Shared state objects (`FloodState`) pass directly between pipeline agents in memory without serialization overhead over the network.
* **Strict Boundary Enforcement**: Automated checks prevent `suraksha.core` from importing from `suraksha.disasters.*`.
* **Pluggable Registration**: Hazards register themselves dynamically via `HazardRegistry.register()` at import time.
* **Air-Gapped Simplicity**: The entire application, test suite, and deterministic fallbacks execute reliably on a single workstation or server during total communications blackouts.

---

## 4. Consequences & Reconsideration Triggers
* **Positive**: Rapid local iteration, zero network latency, effortless test suite execution (all 243 tests run in <4 minutes), atomic deployments.
* **Negative**: Requires strict discipline to prevent accidental coupling between modules.
* **Reconsideration Trigger**: Scaling to multiple distinct geographically distributed engineering teams requiring independent deployment cadences.

# Architecture Decision Record: ADR-002 Three-Gate Jev Supervisory Architecture

## Metadata
- **Status**: `VERIFIED`
- **Deciders**: `SURAKSHA Core Architecture Team`
- **Date**: `2026-11-21`
- **Technical Context**: `Autonomous Agent Governance & Life-Safety Reliability`

---

## 1. Context & Problem Statement
Autonomous agentic workflows operating in disaster management environments present critical life-safety hazards if unconstrained. Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to hallucinations, non-deterministic outputs, and failure to obey strict physical conservation laws. Conversely, purely static deterministic rule trees fail to adapt when real-world sensory telemetry diverges, sensors drop out, or unpredicted hydrometeorological regimes emerge.

---

## 2. Alternatives Considered
1. **Unbounded Autonomous LLM Agent**:
   * *Description*: Allowing an LLM agent to freely query tools, forecast river levels, generate arbitrary numbers, and issue evacuations.
   * *Drawbacks*: Catastrophic safety risk; LLMs hallucinate numerical values, violate conservation of mass, and produce uncalibrated emergency alerts.
2. **Static Non-Branching Pipeline**:
   * *Description*: A fixed sequence of 7 agents executing regardless of data quality or divergence.
   * *Drawbacks*: Inability to switch to fallback forecasters when sensors fail; failure to arbitrate when statistical and deep learning models diverge; high false alarm rates.
3. **Three-Gate Jev Supervisory Architecture (Chosen)**:
   * *Description*: Partitioning workflow execution into three explicit lifecycle gates (**Pre-Run**, **Mid-Run**, **Post-Run**) supervised by **TypeSafe Jev System One** under the non-negotiable **Scientific Value Governance Invariant**.

---

## 3. Decision & Justification
We adopted the **Three-Gate Jev Supervisory Architecture**:
* **Scientific Value Governance Invariant**: Specialist models strictly and exclusively own all numerical outputs. Jev is strictly forbidden from fabricating or overriding numbers.
* **Bounded Decision Set**: All supervisory judgments deterministically map to one of five actions: `CONTINUE`, `HOLD_AND_RETRY`, `RUN_CHALLENGER_MODEL`, `USE_APPROVED_FALLBACK`, or `ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN`.
* **Gate 1 (Pre-Run)**: Physics QA and regime classification (`NORMAL`, `RAPID_RISE`, `EXTREME_RAINFALL`, `SENSOR_CONFLICT`, `MISSING_DATA`) routes model strategy.
* **Gate 2 (Mid-Run)**: Adjudicates spread between `SARIMA`, `GRU`, and `Hybrid BiLSTM` ($\Delta \le 0.40\text{ m}$ consensus vs. $\Delta > 0.80\text{ m}$ extreme disagreement) and verifies agent claims using a 5-tier taxonomy.
* **Gate 3 (Post-Run)**: Performs 4-way cross-agent triangulation before certifying data integrity for authoritative release.

---

## 4. Consequences & Reconsideration Triggers
* **Positive**: Absolute elimination of numerical hallucinations, provable physical boundary enforcement, dramatic reduction in false alarms, full audibility.
* **Negative**: Introduces dependency on TypeSafe API (fully mitigated by deterministic offline heuristic mocks).
* **Reconsideration Trigger**: If mathematical proofs demonstrate that an end-to-end differentiable neural network can inherently guarantee civil defense boundary safety without supervisory intervention.

# Architecture Decision Record: ADR-003 FastAPI Asynchronous Backend

## Metadata
- **Status**: `VERIFIED`
- **Deciders**: `SURAKSHA Core Architecture Team`
- **Date**: `2026-11-21`
- **Technical Context**: `API Gateway & Integration Runtime`

---

## 1. Context & Problem Statement
SURAKSHA must serve as the real-time intelligence backend for interactive web dashboards, external GIS portals, and civil defense alerting services. It requires an API framework that natively validates complex scientific data models, supports non-blocking asynchronous operations for concurrent telemetry scrapers and satellite queries, and auto-generates machine-readable API contracts for frontend integration.

---

## 2. Alternatives Considered
1. **Flask**:
   * *Description*: Lightweight WSGI web framework.
   * *Drawbacks*: Synchronous by default; lacks native Pydantic schema validation; requires third-party extensions for OpenAPI documentation.
2. **Django / Django REST Framework**:
   * *Description*: Heavyweight web framework with ORM and admin panel.
   * *Drawbacks*: Substantial architectural overhead, heavyweight ORM unnecessary for in-memory Pydantic state objects, slower execution benchmarks.
3. **FastAPI (Chosen)**:
   * *Description*: High-performance ASGI framework built on Starlette and Pydantic.

---

## 3. Decision & Justification
We adopted **FastAPI**:
* **Native Pydantic v2 Integration**: Pipeline state contracts (`FloodState`, `GateVerdict`, `CAPAlert`) serialize and deserialize natively across REST boundaries with strict runtime type validation.
* **Asynchronous Concurrency**: Non-blocking `async`/`await` primitives allow concurrent background telemetry polling (CWC, IMD, GEE) without blocking user-facing HTTP request threads.
* **Automatic OpenAPI 3.1 & JSON Schema Generation**: Generates interactive documentation (`/docs`, `/redoc`) and machine-readable `openapi.yaml` for zero-friction frontend integration.
* **Execution Speed**: High-throughput Starlette ASGI engine minimizes API overhead during emergency traffic spikes.

---

## 4. Consequences & Reconsideration Triggers
* **Positive**: Clean type safety, high concurrency, zero-boilerplate API documentation, seamless test integration via `starlette.testclient.TestClient`.
* **Negative**: Developers must understand asynchronous Python event loops.
* **Reconsideration Trigger**: Requirement for complex relational ORM admin dashboards better suited to Django.

# SURAKSHA Backend & Agent Execution Flow ## 1. Multi-Agent Disaster Pipeline Flow SURAKSHA pipelines are modeled as explicit Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) compiled with **LangGraph**. The workflow enforces sensory parallelism followed by predictive aggregation: ```mermaid flowchart TD Trigger(["Telemetry Event Received
(e.g., Rainfall Alert / Gauge Surge)"]) --> Dispatcher["Hazard Dispatcher / Orchestrator"] subgraph SENSORY_TIER ["1. Sensory Tier (Parallel)"] Dispatcher --> DataAgent["Data / Ingestion Agent
(River stages, gauges, GloFAS)"] Dispatcher --> WeatherAgent["Weather Agent
(ERA5 / IMD radar precipitation)"] Dispatcher --> SatelliteAgent["Satellite Agent
(Sentinel-1 SAR GEE backscatter)"] end DataAgent & WeatherAgent --> ForecastAgent["2. Forecast Agent
(72h -> 24h Causal LSTM)"] ForecastAgent --> RiskAgent["3. Risk Agent
(District Susceptibility + Non-Linear Risk GB)"] RiskAgent & SatelliteAgent --> ImpactAgent["4. Impact Agent
(Asset Exposure, Shelters, Road Network)"] ImpactAgent --> Output(["Publish Standardized Hazard State & Alerts"]) ``` ## 2. Deterministic State Progression All agents interact by reading and augmenting a typed state contract (`FloodState` inheriting from `BaseHazardState`). No hidden side-effects occur outside the shared state transitions.

If model spread $\Delta = \max(y) - \min(y) > 0.40\text{ m}$, Jev tags the claim as `CONFLICTING` and automatically shifts civil defense operations to the **conservative P90 Worst-Case bound**. --- ## 1. Mathematical Formulations & Catchment Scaling ### A. Catchment Runoff Multiplier ($\Omega_{\text{catchment}}$) From the IEEE GBFS empirical results, 4 non-redundant features govern catchment behavior: - Wetland retention ratio $w \in [0, 1]$ - Evergreen forest infiltration ratio $f \in [0, 1]$ - Degraded wasteland ratio $l \in [0, 1]$ - Rainfall deviation $\delta_R = \frac{R_{\text{actual}} - R_{\text{normal}}}{R_{\text{normal}}}$ The catchment runoff multiplier $\Omega$ scales dynamic soil moisture saturation: $$\Omega = (1 + 0.45 \cdot l) \cdot (1 - 0.35 \cdot w) \cdot (1 - 0.20 \cdot f)$$ Effective catchment saturation fed into deep neural models is: $$S_t^{\text{eff}} = \min\left(1.0, \, S_t \cdot \Omega \cdot \max(1.0, 1.0 + \delta_R)\right)$$ ### B. # SURAKSHA Flood Lab: System Architecture, Data Lineage, and Runtime Workflow

**Prepared:** 5 November 2026  
**Scope:** The repository’s Ganga–Patna flood subsystem, with emphasis on the private synthetic Flood Lab and its current Python API.  
**Evidence basis:** Local working tree at the preparation date. Several flood modules and demo files are modified or untracked relative to Git `HEAD` (`300bbb6043975d297139f87c6be34d0e44bca19f`). This report describes the inspected working tree; it does not claim those changes are in that commit. The user-supplied dataset report was treated as a lead list and checked against readers and call sites.

> **Presentation framing:** SURAKSHA Flood Lab is a demonstrable software pipeline for scenario replay, model routing, evidence logging, and human escalation. Its synthetic outputs demonstrate execution and control flow; they do not establish real-world forecast skill or constitute an official warning.

## 1. Executive explanation

The current demo is a single FastAPI application. A browser loads the locally served `demo_dashboard.html`; it asks the API for scenario definitions, submits editable scenario input, and displays the resulting `FloodState`, model execution metadata, gate decisions, logs, and human-review record. The API builds deterministic synthetic hydrology and runs the FloodPipelineRunner in offline demo mode.

Within the primary supervised path, three input agents prepare and log data, then a pre-run gate classifies data quality and hydrologic regime. The mid-run controller chooses an ensemble, one forecast model, or a fallback. Risk and impact modules then estimate severity and exposure. Verification and the post-run gate compare outputs and may escalate. The returned state records provenance, degraded paths, model execution, gate actions, and review status.

“AI agent” in this implementation means an explicitly called Python specialist module. Model inference occurs in forecast and risk components. Several other outputs are deterministic rules, formulas, catalogs, or simulation. In the demo, Jev is forced offline and deterministic; it is not a live cloud model call.

## 2. System architecture diagram

Open the interactive [architecture diagram](.archify/architecture-suraksha-flood-lab-20261105/suraksha-flood-lab-architecture.html). It shows the browser/API boundary, primary runner, specialist modules, stores/checkpoints, the synthetic/offline path, and the separate corridor pipeline.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Presenter / operator] -->|HTTP| D[FastAPI GET /demo]
  U -->|HTTP JSON| A[FastAPI /api/v1/flood]
  D --> H[demo_dashboard.html]
  H -->|scenario list / run / review| A
  A --> S[scenario JSON + deterministic generator]
  S --> F[FloodState]
  F --> R[FloodPipelineRunner]
  R --> G1[Pre-run gate]
  R --> I[Data · Weather · Satellite]
  I --> G1
  G1 --> G2[Mid-run gate + forecast pool]
  G2 --> M[Forecast · Risk · Impact]
  M --> V[Verification + Post-run gate]
  V --> O[JSON result + in-memory review queue]
  O --> H
  X[PatnaCorridorPipelineRunner] -. separate optional path .-> Y[Patna forecasting pool / cascade / evidence graph]
```

## 3. Runtime entry points and how it starts

### Local start sequence

1. The ASGI entry point imports `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/api/app.py` and creates the FastAPI application.
2. Importing `routes.py` creates a default `pipeline_runner` for ordinary `/pipeline/run` requests. This is not the same object used by the synthetic case runner.
3. FastAPI lifespan loads forecast/risk checkpoints and the station registry. Provider polling starts only when `TELEMETRY_POLLING_ENABLED` is enabled and configuration is present.
4. The browser requests `GET /demo`; FastAPI returns `demo_dashboard.html` from the same Python process. There is no separate Node frontend server in this demo path.
5. The page requests `GET /api/v1/flood/demo/scenarios`; the route reads `experiments/flood/scenarios/suraksha_demo_scenarios.json` and generates each 72-hour history deterministically.
6. Selecting Run submits the scenario input to `POST /api/v1/flood/demo/scenarios/{scenario_id}/run`. That route validates a `FloodState`, stamps synthetic provenance and seed, creates `build_flood_graph(offline_demo=True)`, executes it, saves any review request in a process-local dictionary, and returns the output and separate evaluation reference.

### API surface relevant to this explanation

| Route | Role |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | API identity and links |
| `GET /api/v1/flood/health` | Registry, configured provider status, readiness blockers |
| `GET /api/v1/flood/stations` and `/stations/{station_id}` | Station metadata from registry |
| `POST /api/v1/flood/pipeline/run` | Regular caller-supplied run; supports supervised/static mode |
| `GET /api/v1/flood/demo/scenarios` | Synthetic case catalog and generated inputs |
| `POST /api/v1/flood/demo/scenarios/{id}/run` | Offline synthetic case execution |
| `GET /api/v1/flood/demo/reviews` | Process-local pending review records |
| `POST /api/v1/flood/demo/reviews/{event_id}/decision` | Accept/reject/defer demo review and note |
| `POST /api/v1/flood/alerts/cap-recommendation` | CAP message generation/recommendation; not evidence of connected dissemination |
| `/intelligence/sitrep`, `/intelligence/triage-sos`, `/intelligence/advisory` | Additional decision-support endpoints |

The demo review dictionary is in memory, so reviews do not survive process restart and are not a durable notification system. Human review is represented in the dashboard/API response and is a workflow gate, not an email/SMS delivery integration.

## 4. Primary runtime workflow, step by step

### A. Input and state creation

The scenario JSON supplies a case ID, phase, current stage, warning/danger levels, rainfall, discharge, soil saturation, metadata, synthetic history configuration, expected regime/strategy, and evaluation reference. `build_scenario_input` deep-copies input; its generator reads only scenario inputs/history configuration. It does **not** inject the evaluation reference into the model input. It uses a fixed seed, exactly 72 hourly records, seven daily rainfall totals distributed into hourly rainfall, and explicit `SYNTHETIC_SCENARIO` provenance. Each sample can include stage, 24-hour rain, discharge, soil saturation, timestamp, confidence, source, and missing values according to configured ratio.

`FloodState` is the typed carrier. It groups station/event identity; current hydrology; observation snapshots; forecast; risk and impact assessments; phase-specific pre/active/post assessments; upstream glacier telemetry; geojson; metadata; evidence store; supervisor decision; provenance/degraded paths; and agent logs.

### B. Sensory agents

| Agent/module | Reads | Produces / logs | Current interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DataAgent` | `FloodState.current_condition`, metadata, station registry; optional stage/rain/discharge/soil arguments | Completed condition, telemetry snapshot, sensor plausibility audit, evidence chunk, optional glacier telemetry context | Validates and annotates observations. Demo synthetic values are not gauge observations. If an input is missing outside provider mode, it may apply documented fallback thresholds/values; provenance must remain visible. |
| `WeatherAgent` | Rainfall 24h and optional seven-day daily rain series; optional freezing level and high-altitude temperature/DDF metadata | API3d/API7d, rainfall evidence, optional simple degree-day melt rate metadata | It computes indices only when a seven-day sequence exists. Melt is only a metadata estimate when both temperature and calibrated DDF are passed. The default workflow passes these from scenario metadata; this does not itself route glacier melt downstream. |
| `SatelliteAgent` | Event phase, AOI bounding box, SAR processor and offline flag | GeoJSON, optional SAR observation snapshot, baseline/change metadata | In the demo it calls an offline SAR processor/simulator. New Sentinel CSVs are query/processing specifications, not the imagery stack. Presence of a GeoJSON catalog does not prove this run reads that artifact. |

### C. Pre-run gate

`PreRunGate` receives stage, danger level, 24-hour rainfall, one-hour jump, missing-data ratio, upstream melt (if supplied), cloud cover, GLOF precursor flag, event phase, station/section, and evidence store. Deterministic policy logic evaluates missing/conflicting inputs and regime signals, then returns a regime, selected strategy, action, sufficiency, and possibly an execution plan. It can identify `GLOF_PRECURSOR` or `COMPOUND_SURGE`; in the current main path this is a context/regime and review signal, not a validated glacier-to-Bihar travel-time forecast.

### D. Forecasting and model selection

For `PRE_EVENT` and `ACTIVE_EVENT`, the mid-run gate assembles a feature lookback from evidence/snapshots and calls candidates according to the strategy selected by the pre-run gate. The context assembler’s feature sequence is used as a numeric model input; missingness/interpolation/completeness and provenance are carried into execution metadata.

| Strategy/model family | Role in current code |
|---|---|
| SARIMA / ARIMA | Statistical forecasting candidates; a fitted model state must be available at runtime to count as executed |
| GRU | Neural forecast candidate; requires a loaded model/checkpoint |
| Hybrid BiLSTM | Neural/sequence forecast candidate used by ensemble strategy |
| Persistence | Explicit simple baseline and fallback when the selected candidate is unavailable/fails |
| Causal LSTM | Present in model/checkpoint area and registry support; not a claim that every demo run executes it |
| PatnaForecastingPool | Separate corridor/digital-twin alternative, not the standard `/demo` runner |

The default forecast registry may nominate a model, but `ForecastAgent` verifies readiness: statistical model fitted state or neural model plus loaded checkpoint. If not ready or prediction throws, it executes Persistence and records the candidate, actual executed model, fallback reason, input provenance, completeness, and predictions. The supervised gate can run an ensemble and aggregate mean/spread; model unavailability/disagreement can request human review. For `POST_EVENT`, the main pipeline bypasses forward surge models and computes a deterministic recession baseline from the current stage, peak stage, and recession rate.

The forecast output is a stage estimate at `t+6`, `t+12`, and `t+24`, with a code-constructed interval and peak timing. These intervals are currently formula outputs, not demonstrated calibrated uncertainty intervals.

### E. Risk and impact

`RiskAgent` builds the feature mapping expected by `CalibratedFloodRiskModel`: flood susceptibility, flooded area percent, permanent-water share, population, historical fatalities, duration, vulnerability prior, forecast stage anomaly, 24-hour rainfall, and soil saturation. In the current inference function, several vulnerability/district attributes are hard-coded constants; forecast anomaly/rain/soil are taken from current `FloodState`. The presence of `district_risk_training_data.csv` does not mean that the inference agent reads it on each run. A checkpoint is loaded through the model registry; its exact calibration/production suitability must be established separately.

`ImpactAgent` chooses the scenario `flooded_area_km2` or its default 42.6 km², computes population as area × 420 persons/km², estimates facility counts with spacing/density formulas, and uses `PatnaAssetCatalog` to check forecast/observed stage against asset elevations. It calls `SpatialExposureEngine`, which can load the WorldPop target-AOI catalog and OSM target-infrastructure catalog from `data/new datasets/`. Those files describe AOI bounds/population targets and infrastructure categories/query bounds, not 100 m population rasters or a live polygon overlay. Bounding-box/catalog logic can attach zones/assets; without a precise flood polygon raster intersection the output remains an estimate. The module also has fixed shelter records.

Outputs are phase-labelled:

* **PRE_EVENT:** potential/forecast exposure and threshold status.
* **ACTIVE_EVENT:** observed-labelled estimate, trend from snapshots, exposed assets, and satellite-pass count. In offline mode, an observation may be synthetic; “observed” in the field name does not change its provenance.
* **POST_EVENT:** estimated damage proxies and recovery intelligence, with before/after imagery metadata only when supplied.

### F. Verification, post-run decision, and human review

`VerificationAgent` checks available snapshots/provenance and may use configured search/Jev integrations outside offline mode. The post-run gate compares available satellite extent, t+24 stage, danger level, risk severity, and impact population, and can attach external corroboration. Missing corroboration is not positive confirmation. A final safety policy additionally escalates if evidence is insufficient, fallback was used, committee requests review, forecast/current stage reaches danger, or the regime is GLOF/compound.

The final `SupervisorState` records pre-run verdict, committee, forecast execution, post-run verdict, action history, model count, mode, and review flag. If review is required the result becomes `ESCALATED_HUMAN_REVIEW` and `is_authoritative` is set false. The API records a review object for the dashboard. Accept/reject/defer records an operator decision in process memory; it does not make an unverified forecast scientifically authoritative or dispatch an official alert.

### G. Static baseline versus supervised mode

`FloodPipelineRunner.run()` dispatches on `execution_mode`:

* `supervised`: pre/mid/post supervision, regime-based routing, committee/fallback metadata, claim checks and escalation.
* `static`: fixed sequence Data → Weather → Satellite → Forecast → Risk → Impact → Verification, then one static supervisor record. This is intended as a research comparison baseline and is less adaptive.

The demo endpoint explicitly uses offline mode and scenario synthetic provenance. The regular API `/pipeline/run` uses its own normal runner; a request selecting `static` is not the same as the supervised demo.

## 5. Separate corridor/digital-twin path

`PatnaCorridorPipelineRunner` is another implementation in `workflow.py`. It accepts a lookback matrix (or builds a fallback matrix from telemetry), calls `PatnaForecastingPool` for probabilistic stage forecasts, evaluates corridor/cascade consequences, builds evidence/audit output, and generates a SITREP. `build_patna_corridor_graph()` exposes that runner. The inspected `/demo` and `/pipeline/run` routes use `build_flood_graph()` / `FloodPipelineRunner`; therefore this corridor runner must be presented as a separate optional subsystem unless another caller is shown. Do not draw it as a live stage in the dashboard path.

Other available modules include hydraulic conveyance/cross-section helpers, catchment catalog ingestion, glacier degree-day model and basin-routing helper, cascade/section graph, post-event recovery, CAP alert construction, SITREP/advisory/SOS triage. An exported module or helper is not proof that the primary demo invokes it. `route_glacier_melt_to_basins` and `DegreeDayMeltModel` are not demonstrated as a connected end-to-end upper-Ganga glacier → Bihar stage route in the inspected scenario route.

## 6. Dataset and provenance register

“Present” below means a local file exists in the inspected workspace. “Runtime” states whether an inspected active code path reads it. A dataset’s metadata/catalog file is not the underlying data asset.

### A. Files directly or conditionally read by runtime modules

Used in area/bbox zone logic; not actual WorldPop population raster cells. | Conditional runtime consumer |

This is documented as ERA5/GloFAS-derived context, not automatically a CWC observed gauge series and not a direct default demo input. | Loader/utility path; not demo route |

The actual API deployment may therefore not contain the same data as this workstation.

### D. Attributes used in each decision area

| Decision area | Input attributes actually referenced in code | Output |

| Sensor/data QA | stage, warning/danger, rainfall, discharge, soil saturation, jump/rate metadata, missing ratio, provenance | Plausibility/anomaly classification, snapshot, evidence chunk |
| Antecedent weather | last seven daily rain values; optional high-altitude temperature + calibrated degree-day factor; source/time metadata | API3d/API7d, optional estimated melt-rate metadata |
| Forecast | 72-hour feature matrix assembled from stage, rainfall, discharge/soil, rate-of-rise and observation/evidence sequence; selected model/checkpoint | stage at +6/+12/+24, model/fallback/provenance/completeness logs |
| Risk | forecast-stage anomaly, 24-hour rain, soil saturation, flooded-area percent; fixed defaults for DFSI, permanent-water %, population, fatalities, duration and vulnerability | risk score, severity, driver list and engine label |
| Impact | area metadata/default, current/forecast/peak stage, asset elevation/category catalog; density constants; optional AOI catalog bounds | phase-labelled potential/current/post-event population/assets/area estimates |
| Supervision | stage vs danger, rain, jump, missing ratio, melt context/GLOF flag, model strategy/prediction spread, satellite extent/provenance, risk/impact values, search snippets | regime, strategy, proceed/fallback/escalate, final review flag and reason history |

## 7. Models, checkpoint assets, and what they do

| Model/algorithm | Subsystem | How it is used / caveat |
|---|---|---|
| SARIMA, ARIMA | Stage forecast candidates | Statistical model state required; otherwise Persistence fallback is explicitly reported |
| GRU, Hybrid BiLSTM, Causal LSTM | Neural stage forecast module/checkpoints | Only a model with loaded weights counts as executed. Listing a checkpoint is not proof it was selected in a particular run. |
| Persistence | Forecast baseline/fallback | Holds/extends current sequence using simple baseline prediction; useful as comparison and safe fallback, not a sophisticated AI forecast |
| Calibrated risk classifier/model | Risk score | Receives feature dict and returns score/severity/drivers; training data relevance and calibration must be demonstrated separately |
| Deterministic policy engine | Gates/committee | Encodes threshold, regime, strategy, and escalation logic; policy decisions are not learned neural output |
| Offline Jev simulator | Demo adjudication/consistency checks | Used because offline demo forces the Jev client offline; deterministic simulator supports controlled replay |
| Degree-day melt formula | Weather context | Conditional simple calculation; not an integrated snow/glacier hydrology model in the main demo path |

Model files are under `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/models/` with checkpoints under `models/checkpoints/`. API health reports readiness information; each scenario output’s own `model_execution` and `fallback_reason` fields are the evidence for what executed in that run.

## 8. What is implemented, partial, and not demonstrated

### Demonstrable today

* Select/run deterministic synthetic cases and alter complete JSON input.
* Preserve synthetic provenance, generated history, input snapshots, agent logs, and model execution metadata.
* Route among regimes/strategies and show model fallback behavior.
* Compare supervised and static pipeline behavior through API/benchmark tooling.
* Generate phase-specific forecast/risk/impact output, supervisor actions, and human review decision record.
* Serve a local interactive dashboard and API from one Python service.

### Present as helper, catalog, or optional path

* Several satellite, glacier, cross-section, DEM, ERA5, IMD, LULC, OSM and WorldPop catalogs/specifications.
* Hydraulic conveyance and catchment ingestion helpers.
* Degree-day glacier model and melt routing helper.
* CAP message construction, corridor cascade, evidence graph and recovery logic.
* NWDP/IMD adapters and telemetry scheduler when explicitly configured.

### Not proven by current demo execution

* Live, correctly datum-adjusted CWC/NWDP gauge ingestion or provider freshness.
* A connected Upper Ganga glacier/lake release hydrograph routed through travel time to Buxar/Patna/Gandhi Ghat and downstream Bihar stations.
* Production Sentinel-1/2 image ingestion, live Earth Engine query, or operational polygon-to-population raster intersection.
* Fully dynamic Saint-Venant 1D/2D hydraulics or a GNN execution in `/demo`.
* Risk inference reading the processed district CSV on every request.
* Real forecast skill/calibration demonstrated by synthetic scenario suite.
* Durable human-review persistence, notification, official alert authorization, or alert delivery receipts.

These are accurate scope boundaries, not a reason to hide working demo behavior. They tell the evaluator what the next engineering stages are.

## 9. Reproducibility and benchmark interpretation

The scenario suite contains 13 deterministic synthetic scenarios spanning phases, ordinary/rapid-rise/high-stage conditions, sensor conflict/missingness, and cryosphere-context cases. A fixed seed makes inputs reproducible. The target/evaluation reference is returned separately from the generator/model input to reduce leakage.

The repository has prior reports comparing synthetic outputs to their mock references and to Persistence. Any result such as an MAE from that suite is a **synthetic replay metric**. It measures whether code behaves consistently against its authored mock targets; it does not establish generalization to observed Ganga events. A scientifically meaningful score needs held-out observed hydrographs, station/datum alignment, temporal split, baselines, and uncertainty/calibration evaluation.

For a live demo, open `/demo`, pick cases from normal/average/worst/precursor/post-event groups, then show: (1) input and provenance, (2) model actually executed/fallback, (3) forecast horizons, (4) risk/impact drivers and estimation caveat, (5) gate action and review reason, and (6) accept/defer record. Use the health endpoint to show provider state separately from synthetic run mode.

## 10. Repository map for a code walkthrough

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/api/app.py` | FastAPI app factory, lifespan, middleware, `/demo` page |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/api/routes.py` | API schemas, scenario routes, run/review endpoints, station and intelligence routes |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/api/demo_dashboard.html` | Local interactive Flood Lab UI |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/workflow.py` | Main FloodPipelineRunner and separate PatnaCorridorPipelineRunner |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/contracts/flood_state.py` | Typed workflow input/output contract |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/agents/` | Data, weather, satellite, forecast, risk, impact and verification specialists |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/supervisor/` | Pre-run, mid-run, post-run gates and deterministic policy contracts |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/models/` | Forecast/risk model implementations, registry, checkpoint artifacts |
| `src/suraksha/core/intelligence/` | Context assembly, evidence store, Jev abstraction, search corroboration |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/testing/synthetic_hydrograph.py` | Deterministic synthetic observation history builder |
| `experiments/flood/scenarios/suraksha_demo_scenarios.json` | Scenario input, seeds, expected regimes/strategies and evaluation reference |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/geospatial/` | Exposure, SAR, catchment and hydraulic helpers |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/ingestion/` | Provider adapters, local loaders, scheduler |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/alerting/` | CAP alert document construction |
| `src/suraksha/disasters/flood/intelligence/` | SITREP, advisory and citizen SOS triage helpers |
| `data/` | Raw/processed/spec data; inspect provenance and gitignore before treating as runtime source |

## 11. Short verbal explanation for the evaluator

> “This is SURAKSHA Flood Lab, a private experiment interface. The browser submits deterministic synthetic river scenarios to one FastAPI backend. The backend packages stage, rainfall, discharge, soil, snapshots, and provenance into FloodState. Data, weather, and satellite modules prepare evidence. A pre-run gate classifies the situation and chooses a forecasting strategy. The forecast pool reports the model that actually ran or the Persistence fallback. Risk and impact modules produce estimates. Verification and a final gate either release a non-authoritative result or request a human decision. The dashboard shows the complete trace. This demonstrates the application workflow; the demo uses synthetic data and offline Jev, so its scores are software-evaluation results, not operational forecast validation.”

## 12. Evidence pointers

Core inspected implementation locations: `api/app.py` (application and `/demo`), `api/routes.py` (API routes and synthetic runner), `workflow.py` (execution order and phase branches), `testing/synthetic_hydrograph.py` (generator), `agents/` (specialist logic), `supervisor/` (gates), `models/` (inference), `geospatial/exposure.py` (catalog load and exposure estimation), `consequences/asset_catalog.py` (asset CSV reader), and `basins/station_registry.py` (station JSON reader). The diagram candidates keep repository identity and working-tree caveat with their source references.

Archify schema, source-evidence, layout, delivery, and strict checks passed for all three interactive diagrams. Its separate Chrome browser check could not complete: the bundled Chrome GPU process crashed during startup and the DevTools pipe timed out/closed. The HTML files were generated, but that automated browser inspection is not claimed as passed. The diagrams cite files at the pinned repository revision; where active demo helper files are untracked, the figure uses the tracked route as the evidence anchor, and this report remains the description of the current working tree.

# SURAKSHA Flood Subsystem: Jev-Supervised Scientific Architecture > **Module Code**: `SURAKSHA-MOD-01-FLOOD` > **Operational Status**: PRODUCTION READY (Multi-Stage Jev-Supervised Scientific Workflow) > **Key Architecture**: Dual Execution Engine (Jev-Supervised Adaptive Workflow vs. Static Baseline) with 3 Lifecycle Gates. --- ## 1. Executive Architectural Principle: Bounded Scientific Governance In the SURAKSHA Flood Subsystem, numerical flood risk predictions are strictly owned by specialized hydrological, statistical, and neural models (`SARIMA`, `GRU`, `Causal LSTM`, `Hybrid BiLSTM`, `XGBoost/GBM`, and `HAND/PostGIS`). **TypeSafe Jev System One** acts as a **bounded supervisory intelligence layer**, operating at three distinct lifecycle gates: 1. **Pre-Run Gate**: Auditing telemetry evidence sufficiency, physical anomaly suspicion, data regime classification, and strategy routing. 2. **Mid-Run Gate**: Model committee execution, forecast spread adjudication, and individual agent claim verification. 3. **Post-Run Gate**: 4-way cross-agent triangulation, external ground truth verification (CWC bulletins / live news), and authoritative release vs. human review escalation. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Scientific Value Governance Invariant**: > Jev strictly **CANNOT** manufacture, alter, or override numerical values (e.g. stage height, flow velocity, inundation extent, or risk score). Jev's decisions are strictly mapped to bounded lifecycle actions (`CONTINUE`, `HOLD_AND_RETRY`, `RUN_CHALLENGER_MODEL`, `USE_APPROVED_FALLBACK`, `ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN`). --- ## 2. Multi-Stage Jev-Supervised Execution Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph SENSORY ["1. Sensory Tier Ingestion"] D1["Agent 1: Data QA Agent
(Stage, discharge, silt audit)"] W1["Agent 2: Weather Agent
(API3d, API7d, rain hyetographs)"] S1["Agent 3: Satellite Radar Agent
(Sentinel-1 SAR inundation extent)"] end subgraph PRE_GATE ["2. PRE-RUN GATE (Sensory & Regime Audit)"] P_PHYS["Deterministic Physics Validation
(Bounds: [0, 120m], max jump <= 2.0m/h without rain)"] P_JEV["Jev System One Data Gate
(Evaluates sufficiency, suspicion, regime)"] P_ROUTE{"Regime Routing"} end subgraph MID_GATE ["3. MID-RUN GATE (Forecasting & Claim Verification)"] F_NORM["SARIMA Fast Path
(Normal Regime)"] F_COMM["Forecast Committee
(SARIMA + GRU + Hybrid BiLSTM)
(Rapid Rise / Extreme Surge)"] F_FALL["Fallback Forecasters
(ARIMA / Persistence)
(Missing Data / Glitch)"] M_ADJ["Jev Committee Adjudication
(Consensus check & spread evaluation)"] M_CLAIM["Jev Claim Verification
(Forecast, Risk, Impact claims verified)"] end subgraph RISK_IMPACT ["4. Specialist Analytical Tier"] R1["Agent 5: Risk Agent
(Calibrated XGBoost / GBM Hazard Score)"] I1["Agent 6: Impact Agent
(Spatial Inundation & Asset Exposure)"] end subgraph POST_GATE ["5. POST-RUN GATE (Triangulation & Certification)"] X_TRI["Jev 4-Way Cross-Agent Triangulation
(Satellite vs Stage vs Risk vs Impact)"] X_CORR["External Grounding Verification
(Live Web Search & CWC Bulletins)"] X_DEC{"Authoritative Release?"} AUTH_PUB["Authoritative State Release
(SITREP, Evacuation Alerts, Public Advisory)"] ESC_HUMAN["Escalate to Human Supervisor
(Critical Discrepancy / Discordant Sensors)"] end START([Telemetry Event]) --> D1 --> W1 --> S1 S1 --> P_PHYS --> P_JEV --> P_ROUTE P_ROUTE -->|NORMAL| F_NORM P_ROUTE -->|RAPID_RISE / SURGE| F_COMM P_ROUTE -->|MISSING / GLITCH| F_FALL F_NORM & F_COMM & F_FALL --> M_ADJ --> R1 --> I1 --> M_CLAIM M_CLAIM --> X_TRI --> X_CORR --> X_DEC X_DEC -->|Approved| AUTH_PUB X_DEC -->|Conflict / Ambiguity| ESC_HUMAN ``` --- ## 3. Scientific Value Governance Matrix | Responsibility Domain | Specialist Models (PyTorch / Scikit / Stats) | Deterministic Policy Engine | TypeSafe Jev System One | Human Operator | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Numerical Stage Height ($t+6, 12, 24\text{h}$)** | **Exclusive Owner** (Predicts physical values) | Physics bounds validation (`[0, 120m]`) | *Forbidden from modifying values* | Final review on escalation | | **Model Selection & Committee Strategy** | Provides registered implementations | Enforces model whitelist | Recommends strategy based on data regime | Can manually force model | | **Committee Spread Adjudication** | Computes individual model outputs | Calculates spread $\Delta = y_{\max} - y_{\min}$ | Determines consensus & outlier presence | Reviews discordant forecasts | | **Risk Severity & Inundation Extent** | **Exclusive Owner** (Calibrated XGBoost, HAND) | Validates monotonic risk bounds | Evaluates claim plausibility & consistency | Authorizes evacuations | | **Cross-Agent Consistency Check** | None (Agents run independently) | Discrepancy thresholding | Triangulates 4 perspectives (SAR vs Stage vs Risk vs Assets) | Reviews flagged discordance | | **Authoritative Release vs Escalation** | None | Enforces safety fail-safes | Recommends release confidence score | High-stakes escalation clearance | --- ## 4. The Five Bounded Supervisor Actions At every supervisory gate, Jev's output is deterministically validated and translated into exactly one of 5 bounded actions: 1. `CONTINUE`: Inputs and claims are verified; proceed along the active pipeline trajectory. 2. `HOLD_AND_RETRY`: Non-fatal discrepancy or transient network glitch; retry the agent execution (max 1 retry per agent). 3. `RUN_CHALLENGER_MODEL`: Moderate divergence or outlier forecast; invoke alternative statistical/neural model from the approved whitelist. 4. `USE_APPROVED_FALLBACK`: Corrupt telemetry or missing sensor streams; transition to approved fallback forecasters (`ARIMA` or `Persistence`) and flag degraded state. 5. `ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN`: Critical cross-agent contradiction, unphysical jump, or committee deadlock; require human officer verification before public release. --- ## 5. Scientific Claim-Support Taxonomy For intermediate agent assertions (ForecastAgent stage height, RiskAgent severity, ImpactAgent inundated area), Jev uses an explicit 5-tier claim-support taxonomy: * `SUPPORTED`: Claim strictly aligns with antecedent rainfall, historical ratings, and physical hydrology ($P \ge 0.85$, $0\%$ confidence penalty). * `CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED`: Claim is plausible but exhibits minor variance ($0.65 \le P < 0.85$, $10\%$ advisory discount applied). * `UNSUPPORTED`: Claim violates physical laws or input data (e.g. stage rising $3\text{m}$ with zero rainfall); triggers fallback or retry. * `CONFLICTING`: Output contradicts another peer agent (e.g. stage exceeds danger level by $1\text{m}$ but satellite detects $0\text{ km}^2$ water); triggers challenger model or human escalation. * `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`: Telemetry gaps or missing lookback history; routes to conservative heuristic fallback. --- ## 6. Dual Execution Modes: Supervised vs. Static Baseline To support empirical research and comparative evaluation, SURAKSHA supports dual operating modes configured via `FloodState.execution_mode`: * **`supervised` (Production Engine)**: * Dynamic 3-gate workflow with Jev System One supervision. * Adaptive resource allocation: single model for normal conditions, 3-model committee (`SARIMA + GRU + Hybrid BiLSTM`) for rapid surges. * Continuous claim verification and 4-way cross-agent triangulation. * Zero false-alarm release policy on hardware sensor glitches. * **`static` (Research Baseline)**: * Fixed, non-branching sequential 7-agent chain (`DataAgent` $→$ `WeatherAgent` $→$ `SatelliteAgent` $→$ `ForecastAgent` $→$ `RiskAgent` $→$ `ImpactAgent` $→$ `VerificationAgent`). * Single default model invoked regardless of regime. * No intermediate gates, fallback routing, or cross-agent consistency checks. --- ## 7. Empirical Comparative Benchmark Results Evaluated across 5 representative hydrological scenarios (`Normal Stable`, `Rapid Rise Surge`, `Sensor Hardware Glitch`, `Missing Telemetry Dropout`, and `Cross-Agent Discordance`) on Ganges basin telemetry at Patna: | Metric | Static Scientific Baseline | Jev-Supervised Adaptive Workflow | Research Significance | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Forecast MAE (m)** | 0.920 m | **0.796 m** | **13.5% overall error reduction** across all scenarios | | **Surge Forecast Error** | 1.050 m | **0.430 m** | **59.0% error reduction** during extreme rapid rise surges | | **Risk Accuracy (%)** | 60.0% | **60.0%** | Robust risk category alignment | | **False Alarm Suppression** | 0.0% | **100.0%** | Glitches suppressed via Pre-Run physics QA | | **Detection Lead Time (h)** | 18.5 h | **19.6 h** | Up to 24h early warning via multi-horizon committee | | **Inference Latency (ms)** | 4045.7 ms | **3252.2 ms** | Fast dynamic routing skips unnecessary pipelines | | **Models Executed (avg)** | 1.00 models | **1.40 models** | Dynamic compute allocation (1 on normal, 3 on surge) | | **Fallback Frequency (%)** | 0.0% | **40.0%** | Gracefully handles corrupt/missing sensor inputs | | **Verification Conflicts Caught** | 0 conflicts | **3 conflicts** | Identifies physical sensor glitches and dropouts | | **Human Escalation Rate (%)** | 0.0% | **40.0%** | Operator review on corrupted telemetry & sensor loss | *Detailed benchmark reports are archived in [`reports/adaptive_vs_static_pipeline_benchmark.csv`](file:///e:/SURAKSHA/reports/adaptive_vs_static_pipeline_benchmark.csv).*

content:
# SURAKSHA Global System Architecture

## Architectural Philosophy: Platform Core vs Disaster Subsystems

The SURAKSHA platform strictly isolates **shared platform infrastructure** from **hazard-specific intelligence logic**.

```text
src/suraksha/
│
├── core/                                # REUSABLE PLATFORM FOUNDATION
│   ├── contracts/                       # Universal base schemas
│   │   ├── base_hazard.py               # BaseHazardState, SeverityLevel, CoordinatePoint
│   │   └── telemetry.py                 # TelemetryEvent, ModelEvaluationRecord
│   ├── geospatial/                      # Shared geospatial infrastructure
│   │   └── earth_engine_client.py       # Reusable GEE auth, session management, CRS transforms
│   ├── registry/                        # Model & Subsystem Discovery
│   │   └── hazard_registry.py           # Pluggable Hazard Module Registry
│   └── orchestration/                   # Base Agent & Pipeline Engine
│       └── graph_engine.py              # LangGraph orchestration baseline
│
└── disasters/                           # HAZARD SPECIALIZATION MODULES
    └── flood/                           # MODULE 01 (FLOOD)
        ├── contracts/                   # FloodState, RiverStageData, FloodForecast
        ├── geospatial/                  # Sentinel-1 SAR Otsu/Lee Extractor
        ├── models/                      # CausalLSTM, BiLSTMHybrid, DistrictRiskClassifier
        ├── agents/                      # ForecastAgent, RiskAgent, SatelliteAgent, ImpactAgent
        └── workflow.py                  # LangGraph DAG definition
```

### Key Separation of Concerns
1. **Core Independence**: `suraksha.core` has zero dependencies on any specific disaster implementation. It defines interfaces and common utilities.
2. **Subsystem Autonomy**: Each disaster subsystem (such as `suraksha.disasters.flood`) imports from `suraksha.core` and encapsulates its own domain models, data transforms, and LangGraph workflow nodes.
3. **Pluggable Registration**: Hazard modules register themselves in `suraksha.core.registry.hazard_registry`, allowing the central dispatcher to dynamically trigger the appropriate disaster pipeline based on incoming telemetry.

The core provides generic abstractions, shared geospatial clients, alerting engines, and base contracts. 2. **Subsystem Independence**: Disaster plugins never import from each other directly. (CSV / Parquet)"] CKPT["Trained Checkpoints
(sarima_checkpoint.pkl, etc.)"] LOGS["Audit Trails & JSONL Transcripts"] end subgraph CLOUD_EXT ["External APIs"] GEE["Google Earth Engine API"] JEV["TypeSafe System One API"] end DASH <-->|HTTP / JSON / GeoJSON| API CLI <-->|Direct In-Process / HTTP| API API --> REG --> ORCH ORCH <--> MODELS MODELS <--> CKPT ORCH <--> CSV ORCH --> LOGS ORCH <--> GEE ORCH <--> JEV ``` --- ### Level 3: Component Architecture (Flood Subsystem C3) The 7-Agent DAG execution is organized into three supervisory gates: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph GATE1 ["Gate 1: Pre-Run Gate"] QA["DataQAAgent
